title: Mobility patterns: step() infinite-loops on sub-microsecond leg times
description: int(distance/speed*1e6) truncates to 0 when leg time < 1us (legal configs pass validation), so remaining_us never decreases. ManhattanGrid.step (mobility.py:782) hangs DETERMINISTICALLY when spacing_m/speed_m_s < 1e-6. GroupMobility (:442) and RPGM (:646) hang with pause_time_us=0 (PAUSED<->MOVING ping-pong consumes 0us). RandomWaypoint._handle_moving (:166) has the same latent truncation (pre-existing, probabilistic-only). Fix: max(1, leg_us) floor or rational time accounting; also cap per-step work or validate speed/spacing ratio. Tests: giant-dt hang regression for all four patterns.
close_reason: Fixed: sub-us legs charge true float time (int() truncation was the stall), >=1us legs keep exact int semantics (bit-identical trajectories verified), 100k-iteration cap per step() bounds giant-dt. 4 new giant-dt regression tests (one per pattern, pytest-timeout), full sim suite 1644 passed, mypy clean on file, ruff clean. Review findings filed as cszg (jitter loop hang), ohw4 (NaN/inf validation), 3x2e (P3 batch).
